pending_part_2.voiceover_script: In Part One, we explored the gruesome, unexplained deaths of nine hikers on Dead Mountain... but when declassified KGB archives finally leaked decades later, investigators uncovered a terrifying cover-up. The strange radiation on their clothing matched top-secret Soviet parachute mine tests conducted nearby. Witnesses reported glowing orange spheres drifting across the Ural sky the exact night the hikers perished, perfectly matching military ordnance misfires. Meteorologists suggest a rare, violent infrasonic vortex—a silent atmospheric wave known as a Kármán vortex street—could have triggered sudden panic, driving the group temporarily insane from pressure and fear. Yet, none of these theories fully explain the missing tongue or the unnatural bodily trauma. To this day, the ultimate fate of the Dyatlov group remains an open, bleeding wound in history.
